- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.06) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.22) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward more aggressively.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +0.5–1.0% in 1–2 days); cap forecast peaks at 10–15% above recent high.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to reverse; add slight upward bias in next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price volatility in early forecast window; increase early forecast by 0.5–1.0% relative to 15-day average.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.06) and price is stable, model often drifts downward; add 0.1–0.3% upward bias to prevent premature decline.
